name: How to Plan a Garage Drywall Installation Project: Step-by-Step Process

step.name: Step 1: Inspect framing, wiring, and rough-in utilities
step.text: Verify that all wall studs, ceiling joists, electrical wiring, and rough plumbing are fully inspected, secured, and ready to be enclosed. Check for moisture or bowed studs that need straightening before any board goes up.

step.name: Step 2: Verify local fire-separation code requirements
step.text: Check whether walls or ceilings border occupied living spaces, which determines whether 5/8-inch Type X gypsum board or standard panels are required. Confirm local building amendments before ordering materials.

step.name: Step 3: Measure, cut, and hang ceiling panels first
step.text: Position drywall sheets across ceiling joists using proper drywall lifts and secure them with code-compliant fasteners. Stagger all butt joints and ensure tight fits around light boxes and garage door opener framing.

step.name: Step 4: Install wall drywall sheets horizontally
step.text: Hang upper wall panels tight against the ceiling before securing bottom rows. Keep boards lifted slightly off the concrete floor slab to avoid moisture wicking from garage floor washdowns or melting snow.

step.name: Step 5: Seal mechanical and electrical penetrations
step.text: Apply approved fire-rated sealants around electrical junction boxes, piping, and ducts that pass through the home-to-garage separation barrier. Never leave open gaps behind outlet covers.

step.name: Step 6: Tape, mud, and finish all fastener heads and seams
step.text: Apply joint tape and successive coats of joint compound across all seams and screw indentations. Feather edges cleanly and sand smooth once dry to prepare the surface for primer and paint.
